## Independent review (not inherited approval)

This is a fresh material-amendment review of correlation `GUARD-REVIEW-203e44225a3e40c9996649f07fcc6921`. INPUT-2 correctly sets `material_amendment_is_not_covered_by_historical_review: true`, `status: pending_amendment_review`, `produced_if_gates: []`, and records that round 4 was not a usable four-seat result (Fable produced no review; Gemini’s terminal line was nonconforming). Historical runner state is untouched (`runner_state_modified: false`, `runner_verification_claimed: false`). No IF gate is produced here. GUARD implementation tests were not requested and are not due as a condition of reviewing this plan.

The amendment is largely aligned with S1 and S2: hosted Ubuntu full-gate topology, digest-pinned disposable SQL, `tested_source_sha` from event context (PR head vs `github.sha`), no `pull_request_target`, same gate for PR/main/release, `guard-required` failure on skipped/cancelled/failed verification, retained-tarball publication without rebuild/repack, recording-only TRIAGE acceptance allowlist, CASE-HY-6 exactly three type-only edges, PREP remaining on source repair/license, COORD remaining on RPC/behavior, SHIP remaining on OIDC/registry, no GUARD release dispatch.

## Prioritized findings

**P1 — Fixture credentials in the single full root suite can change non-GUARD tests.**  
`pnpm verify` launches the root suite once with admitted `GUARD_TEST_DATABASE_URL` (and “complete owned-fixture connection parameters”) after stripping ambient `PG*`/`SUPABASE_*`/`DATABASE_URL`. That same process also collects package tests, including the four process suites whose DATA/COORD assertions must stay unchanged. The plan never requires worker/subprocess isolation so that only `tests/guard/*.db.test.ts` may read the fixture URL. As written, an existing test that keys off `GUARD_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, `PGHOST`, or related variables could unskip, connect, or change behavior. That contradicts “DATA/COORD behavioral assertions remain unchanged,” “COORD must select/test its own caller roles,” and “Neither accepts ambient credentials.” Freeze one of: (a) DB cases in a child with the URL, rest of the suite stripped, or (b) an explicit test that non-DB collected files ignore fixture env and do not change skip/pass counts.

**P2 — Setup falsifiers vs one admitted fixture are unspecified in the same `tests/guard/**` tree.**  
Interface freeze: one admitted fixture, one root suite, focused commands are not substitutes. SL-0 also requires live negative setup controls (unreachable port, invalid migration, missing role, unexpected attributes, missing function) using temporary migration dirs and owned containers. Root config collects `tests/guard`. If those falsifiers run inside verify’s single suite, they can destroy or replace the admitted fixture, fight ports, or be skipped to keep the gate green. If they run only under `pnpm test:guard`, verify does not path-enter them and EC-GUARD-1/2 diverge. State that negative setup controls use isolated disposable instances, cannot mutate the admitted gate fixture, and that an orchestration path which drops them still fails the real gate.

**P3 — Lint scope vs allowed edits on the four process suites is contradictory.**  
`tsconfig.guard.json` type-aware `no-floating-promises` includes the four named process suites. Impl on those files is limited to timeout/readiness/cleanup; “arbitrary void suppressions” and production-logic mutation are forbidden. Those files are not in the source appendix, so floating promises are unproven — but if they exist, SL-0 cannot both add the rule and stay inside the edit limit. Explicitly allow await-only edits that do not change DATA/COORD assertions, or exclude those four files from the new rule until a later owner.

**P4 — Real publication job is not frozen off the legacy pack path.**  
S6 always packs with `pnpm pack`. The amendment adds mutually exclusive `--verified-artifact` and an E404 stub so existing-version skips are not treated as proof. Publication text says download the same run’s artifact and publish those tarballs without packing. It does not freeze `publish.yml`’s id-token job to `--verified-artifact` only, nor reject caller-supplied artifact IDs on `workflow_dispatch`. Legacy `<package-directory>` mode remaining for compatibility is fine; a real npm job that still packs would break tested-vs-published identity. Freeze: id-token job `needs` the producing verify job, uses only that run’s artifact ID, and never `pnpm pack`.

**P5 — Missing named identity for “designated integration cases actually executed.”**  
The selector `tests/guard/*.db.test.ts` plus “empty focused execution passing” falsifies EC-GUARD-2, but the full gate’s execution assertion has no frozen case names/count. Require a manifest of required DB case IDs (or a fail-closed count bound to files SL-0 owns) so a rename/empty glob cannot skip-green.

**P6 — Pre-implementation unowned-test inventory for CASE-HY-6.**  
S3–S5 and the receipt literal scan agree on three verbatim `import type` edges; S9 does not check import syntax; AST evasion remains a GUARD test duty. Owned surfaces for the baseline are `tests/guard/**` and `scripts/check-dependency-boundaries.mjs`. Any unowned package test that still demands zero relative transport imports would fail the full gate, and CASE-HY-6 forbids deferring a failing gate to PREP. The parent already requires ownership amendment before new source writes; record an explicit pre-SL-0 search of unowned tests that would fail under the three-edge baseline.

## Not blockers (due in SL-0/SL-2 or later owners)

- Positive/negative SQL admission, role attributes (`guard_client` `NOINHERIT` + `SET ROLE service_role` on a finally-closed probe), libpq scrub including `PGHOSTADDR`/`PGSERVICEFILE`/`PGPASSFILE`/`PGOPTIONS`/`PGSSLMODE`, image/platform digest equality, hung-child/null-status/process-group controls, workflow secret/ref falsifiers, `guard-required` observation, hosted PR-head `pnpm verify`.
- S7 is truncated; preserving remaining smoke assertions is an SL-0 file-owned duty, not PREP all-package proof.
- S8 `SECURITY DEFINER` query of `coordination_query_leases('{}'::jsonb)` is not RLS or hosted Supabase proof; do not execute `coordination_acquire_lease` or `coordination_send_message`; COORD owns RPC behavior.
- No-id-token rehearsal is not OIDC/registry proof; that remains SHIP.
- 2026-09-12 baseline (348 pass, one live-smoke skip, build-before-test) is not PostgreSQL or retained-tarball proof.
- License, three-edge source repair, CASE-HY-4 closure, runner repair, and release dispatch are correctly deferred.
- Literal `rg` inventory is not AST proof; the plan already says that.

## Recording-only acceptance

The pending receipt is intentional. Allowlisted paths (`status`, `review.amendment_panel`, `review.current_panel`, `criteria.EC-TRIAGE-3`, `produced_if_gates`, `accepted_at`) plus external before/after digest binding at `plans/evidence/v2/TRIAGE-acceptance-binding.json` are the only post-panel writes. `review.current_panel` is allowlisted and currently absent, which is fine. Anything outside that allowlist, including plan/SQL/ownership/test-requirement fixes for P1–P4, is a material amendment and needs a new panel. Accepting TRIAGE must not produce IF-0-GUARD-2. User-authorized manual orchestration does not waive tests, branch protection, publication integrity, or named seats. Unavailable/refusing seats are not approval; Fable remains subscription TUI.

Close P1–P4 in the plan text before implementation. P5–P6 can be SL-0 test/ownership obligations if stated now. Do not treat this seat as four-seat reconciliation.

This review covers the supplied amendment and bounded source evidence. The full historical audit corpus is not supplied, and declared hashes have not been independently recomputed.

**No blocking plan-amendment defect is established.** One nonblocking clarification would improve implementation precision:

1. **Low priority — explicitly include main-push identity mapping.** SL-0 specifies `tested_source_sha` for pull requests, releases and dispatches, but omits an explicit mapping for the main-push event despite requiring main verification. State that push uses `github.sha`, and include that event in the identity-routing falsifier. The existing requirement to verify main through the shared gate makes this a clarification of intended behavior.

The substantive review supports proceeding to current-candidate reconciliation:

- **Ownership is sufficiently bounded.** SL-0 owns the transport smoke, publication helper, workflow wiring, tooling configuration and named process suites. Parent ownership covers the final SQL receipt and TRIAGE recording documents. S3–S5 support the three specifically identified imports; S9 confirms that the existing checker validates membership rather than import syntax. Recursive enforcement belongs to SL-0, while source repair remains PREP-owned.

- **SQL admission and privilege requirements are coherent.** Fixture ownership, environment scrubbing, read-only admission before bootstrap, explicit installer attributes and the separate `guard_client` identity address the relevant boundaries. The dedicated, finally-closed `SET ROLE` probe prevents that connection from becoming the default integration identity. S8 supports the query’s visible declaration and shape; it does not establish complete migration execution, RLS behavior or hosted Supabase correctness.

- **Artifact identity and CI failure propagation are adequately specified.** The plan requires retained tarballs, same-run artifact identity, source/input/content checks before publication effects, and a non-skip E404 falsifier that exercises the retained-artifact path. Signal/null-status controls, suppressed DB collection, stage failures and failed/skipped/cancelled verification must fail the gate. Hosted rehearsal remains distinct from SHIP’s real OIDC and registry evidence.

- **The pending receipt and recording procedure are appropriate.** The external before/after digest binding avoids self-reference. The recording allowlist operates alongside immutable candidate inputs, mandatory current-input four-seat review and coordinator reconciliation. Historical reviews cannot approve this amendment, and historical runner state remains untouched.

The specified implementation tests and hosted observations are obligations for SL-0/SL-2, not prerequisites to approving this plan. Later behavioral and packaging findings retain their named owners. This review records independent amendment evidence only; it grants no phase acceptance or publication authority.

AGREE
